title: One Hand, Five Labels: A Critical Examination of the Five-Scribe Hypothesis for the Voynich Manuscript
summary: Version 5 of this open preprint examines the use of glyph outlines, Currier classes, and illustration sections in Davis's five-scribe attribution. It presents selected examples of within-folio shape variation and proposes that spacing and writing habits may account for some of the differences. Its accompanying image annotations permit inspection of individual glyph crops.
established: Figure 1 uses six word crops from f23v. Four contain EVA k, and the bottom row illustrates three n terminations. The examples show variation in the appearance of k crossbars and n terminations within the folio assigned to Scribe 1. They are chosen illustrations, with no reported random sample or per-folio count of the specific variants.

Section 4 derives about 44 uploaded images and 369 glyph annotations from earlier presentation and application screenshots. These describe the evidence visible in those materials. The amount of material Davis reviewed outside the screenshots is undetermined.

Sections 5.2 and 5.3 contrast selected Herbal A and pharmaceutical letter shapes and suggest an association between available writing space and the detached or attached plume on EVA sh. The claim is qualitative. The preprint provides neither a spacing-matched estimate nor a measured frequency for the plume variants.

The companion Archetype dump contains 1,684 distinct graphs linked through annotations to 201 of 203 image records. The eight archival hand bins are Davis-derived regional categories. The selected graph totals are 854 iin, 32 in, 432 k, 348 sh, and 18 unusual forms.

The dump records the glyph group and image geometry but has no populated graph-level feature tables for the proposed shape variants. All 39 Pharma-bin entries are sh. The f2r versus f99r iin contrast is described in the preprint, so testing it needs new independent iin annotations rather than tabulating the Pharma bin.

open.question: Does local writing space predict whether the plume of EVA sh touches its bench after accounting for Currier group, line position and illustration section?
open.check: Choose paragraph-text candidates from the native scans without using the archive's existing sh crops for selection. Before decoding page or hand labels, have two readers independently score visible plume attachment, ambiguous contact, line height and adjacent spacing. Include well-supported same-Currier cross-hand and same-assigned-hand cross-section comparisons where available. Hold out entire physical bifolios when comparing a spacing-and-position model with the same model plus existing hand labels. Report rater agreement, the number of eligible folios and unscorable crops, and where the matched support is inadequate.

evidence.audit_method: Read the PostgreSQL COPY text in digipal_project/archetype.sql. Join annotation.image_id to image.id and annotation.graph_id to graph.id. Join graph.idiograph_id through idiograph.allograph_id to allograph.name and graph.hand_id to hand.label. Count distinct graph and image identifiers; these are annotation coverage counts.
